summary: Tip: review records access and transfers this shift. Findings: (1) Data staging (incident allegation, confident ~0.85): jpark's console session on workstation (session 74, 11:14-11:20 UTC) ran clinic-export of patients_full to /tmp/.font-unix/idx-3e08.bin at 11:15:15; records app logged export_bulk of 20,578,812 bytes at 11:15:16 from 10.20.1.21. (2) Policy-violating transfer (incident allegation, ~0.85): at 11:18:27-11:18:40 workstation sent 20,582,305 bytes to 10.20.9.87:8080 via curl upload of the staged file; destination is not on the approved list and exceeds the 5 MB threshold. Tap flow is an independent witness. (3) Unexplained local absence (downgraded from removal): one collector-retained auth.log line (seq 29, jpark login 11:14:18) is missing from the workstation's local auth.log. This is not established as deletion because the host file is writable and no deletion event was found. (4) Benign: 185 records access.log lines absent 06:22-08:59 are explained by the scheduled 09:00 rotation (keep 0, archived off-host). (5) Benign: 11:59 transfer from records to approved backup NAS stor-nas-01 (10.20.0.45) is policy-consistent. Attribution: account jpark was used; human operator not established. Account is a credential, not a person, and the console credential may be shared or written down.

Was the seq 29 auth.log line deleted deliberately or lost in a local write fault?
Were any other records or files removed from the workstation or records hosts? Auth.log.1 and the shell histories are host-local and writable.
